title: Improved Bounds for Longer Reverse Cycle Walking
summary: Security bounds have been proved for reverse 2-cycle walking; whether variants with cycle length greater than two yield better bounds remains open.

formal_statement.body: Reverse $2$-cycle walking has been analyzed for security, while reverse cycle walking also generalizes to reverse $t$-cycle walking for $t>2$. Determine whether any such longer-cycle variant yields better bounds than those proved for reverse $2$-cycle walking.

scope.domain: Security analysis of reverse cycle-walking constructions.
parameters: t: cycle length in reverse t-cycle walking, with values greater than 2 defining the longer-cycle variants
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether any reverse t-cycle walking variant for t greater than 2 yields better bounds than those proved for reverse 2-cycle walking.

citations.label: Reverse Cycle Walking and Its Applications

progress.summary: The paper reports a security analysis of reverse 2-cycle walking and notes its generalization to longer cycles. It asks whether choosing t greater than 2 can improve the bounds proved there.
citation_labels: Sarah Miracle et al., Reverse Cycle Walking and Its Applications
